title: An ATPγS recycling strategy for practical biocatalytic thiophosphorylation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the main supplementary PDF (30,061,774 bytes, free, no login) and extracted its text with pdfminer. Read the table of contents, the whole 'Optimization of Reaction Conditions' section (Tables S1-S6 visible: 3, 6, 11, 6, 5 and 9 entries respectively) and the product characterization section. Counted 18 supplementary tables in total, 75 HRMS (high-resolution mass spectrometry) records and 84 occurrences of the word 'yield' in the characterization pages. Also checked sizes of the other two supplementary PDFs (1.4 MB and 3.2 MB) and confirmed the data availability statement on the Nature page.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The scope figures in the main text are behind Nature's paywall, so the exact number of substrates shown there is from the abstract's description plus the supplementary characterization count, not from the main figures. No machine-readable file of any kind exists for this paper.

a1_downloadable.note: The three supplementary PDFs download freely without a login (30 MB, 1.4 MB, 3.2 MB), but the article itself is subscription-only and the data availability statement says only 'All data are available in the main text or the supplementary materials'. No repository deposit: Europe PMC shows no accessions, no PMC record, and a Zenodo search on the topic returned nothing related.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, checked in the files. The label (reaction yield) exists only as numbers printed inside PDF tables and hand-drawn reaction schemes, e.g. Table S3's '31P NMR yield' column of 11 entries. There is no CSV, TSV or spreadsheet anywhere; every value would have to be transcribed by hand from a PDF, and many are given as text ('trace', 'LC-MS detected, low NMR yield').

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL, checked in the files. Substrates and products are drawn as chemical structure images in the PDF; no SMILES (a text format for molecules) or InChI strings appear anywhere in the extracted text. Every input molecule would have to be redrawn or hand-encoded, and enzymes are named by abbreviation (Ta-NK, Hb-CK) with sequences buried in a 25-page text section.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated clearly where values appear: '31P NMR yield' in percent with methyl phosphonic acid as internal standard, concentrations in mM, loadings in mol%, temperature in °C, time in hours.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, checked in the files. 18 supplementary tables with roughly 3-11 entries each, plus about 75 characterized products. Total measured data points are on the order of 100-200, far below the ~1,500-row bar (or ~400 for classification). This is a synthetic methodology paper, not a dataset.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; the problem is that it is too small, not too big.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No count to disagree about; the supplementary tables are internally consistent with the abstract's description of nucleoside monothiophosphates, cyclic monophosphorothioates and thiophosphorylated peptides.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are real physical measurements: quantitative phosphorus-31 nuclear magnetic resonance (31P NMR) yields against an internal standard, plus isolated yields and HRMS confirmation. No model-derived labels. This is the one Part A item the paper does well.

existing_models.name: Phosformer-ST, a transformer model that predicts which kinase phosphorylates which serine/threonine site
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported as state of the art for kinase-substrate specificity by its authors; I did not retrieve the exact number or split, only the GitHub availability (github.com/esbgkannan/Phosformer-ST) from search results.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved — I did not open the paper because Part A had already failed.

existing_models.name: ESP (Enzyme Substrate Prediction), a general model for whether a small molecule is a substrate of an enzyme
existing_models.score_and_split: Authors report over 90% accuracy on independent test data; number taken from a search summary, not from the paper itself.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) for the kinases plus ChemBERTa (a molecule language model) for the substrates would be the natural pair
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would be plenty, but with ~100-200 hand-transcribed data points there is nothing to fit a head on.
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed, ChemBERTa is permissive; irrelevant here because the data does not support training.

integration.partner_dataset: BRENDA or Rhea (enzyme reaction and kinetics databases) keyed on EC number, in principle
integration.join_key: EC number or UniProt accession — but neither appears as a machine-readable field in this paper's supplement, only enzyme nicknames like Ta-NK in prose.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written usefully: with a hundred-odd yields from one lab on one reaction type, joining to a large enzyme database adds breadth to nothing.

controls.positive_control: None available — too few measurements to hold anything out.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at this sample size.
controls.external_validation: No second source: biocatalytic thiophosphorylation yields are not tabulated in any public database I could find.

honest_claim_h3: Any model built here could only claim 'predicts the 31P NMR yield of thiophosphorylation among the roughly 100 substrate/condition combinations one lab chose to publish, nearly all of which worked' — which is a claim about one lab's reporting habits, not about chemistry.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use substrate structure and reaction conditions to predict the yield of an enzyme-catalysed thiophosphorylation reaction.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one reaction: a drawn substrate molecule, the kinase used, and conditions (pH, temperature, time, enzyme loading, concentration). I counted roughly 100-200 such reactions across 18 supplementary tables and ~75 characterized products — all from this single paper.
plain_idea.predict: The percentage yield of the thiophosphorylated product, measured by quantitative phosphorus-31 nuclear magnetic resonance against an internal standard, or isolated yield after purification.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If it worked, process chemists could pick a kinase and conditions for a new thiophosphate target without screening; but with a hundred data points, all from successful published reactions, it cannot work.

ml_idea: The only idea the data supports — predict thiophosphorylation yield from substrate structure and conditions — dies on sample size and format. The genuinely interesting adjacent question (which kinases accept which non-native nucleoside and peptide substrates) would need a dedicated screening dataset that this paper does not provide.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed beyond the PDF text extraction, which took about a minute per 70 pages. The 20 hours is hand-transcribing ~150 yields and drawing ~75 structures into SMILES from PDF images.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the measured yields in the supplementary tables. I did: ~100-200, an order of magnitude short of what any model needs.

verdict_reason: A synthetic chemistry methods paper with no dataset. Verified in the supplementary PDF: roughly 100-200 reaction yields spread over 18 tables, molecules present only as drawn structures (no SMILES), labels only as numbers printed in PDF tables, and censored entries like 'trace' and '>95%'. Fails A2 (label is not a column in any file), A3 (inputs are images, not machine-readable structures) and A5 (far under 1,500 rows). The measurements themselves are honest physical ones (A8 passes), which is the only bright spot.
